definition.def: If you describe someone as dynamic, you approve of them because they are full of energy or full of new and exciting ideas. [approval]
examples: He seemed a dynamic and energetic leader.
Marcus was handsome, dynamic and ambitious.

definition.def: If you describe something as dynamic, you approve of it because it is very active and energetic. [approval]
examples: South Asia was known as the most dynamic economic region in the world.
...90 minutes of dynamic Indian folk dance.

definition.def: A dynamic process is one that constantly changes and progresses.
The dynamic of a system or process is the force that causes it to change or progress.
examples: The dynamic of the market demands constant change and adjustment.

definition.def: The dynamics of a situation or group of people are the opposing forces within it that cause it to change.
examples: The interchange of ideas aids an understanding of family dynamics.

definition.def: Dynamics are forces which produce power or movement. [technical]
examples: Scientists observe the same dynamics in fluids.

definition.def: Dynamics is the scientific study of motion, energy, and forces.
examples: His idea was to apply geometry to dynamics.
